traceability.notes:
The story `docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` is fully implemented.
Both ESLint rules `require-story-annotation` and `require-req-annotation` are present, wired into the plugin, and use a shared configuration model (`DEFAULT_SCOPE`, `EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES`, and `shouldProcessNode`) so they enforce their respective annotations on the same set of function-like constructs: FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, and TSMethodSignature. Arrow functions are explicitly not included in the default scope and are not enforced by either rule, satisfying the requirement that arrow functions are excluded by default.
JSDoc and comment parsing for @story and @req use consistent, robust helpers, with common SourceCode APIs and additional heuristics for nearby comments and text windows. Both rules enforce the presence of their annotations when in scope, support the same configurable `scope` and `exportPriority` semantics, and report errors at the function identifier or nearest equivalent node. TypeScript-specific constructs (TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature, TS function expressions) are explicitly supported and thoroughly tested via shared TS RuleTester options and the `annotation-checker` helper.
Comprehensive Jest RuleTester suites validate correct and incorrect behavior across all required node types, configuration options, and TypeScript integration. Rule documentation files provide user-facing descriptions, configuration schemas, and examples aligned with the story’s requirements. All tests pass, and the rules are integrated into the plugin’s recommended and strict configurations. Together, this provides concrete evidence that all acceptance criteria and listed technical requirements for Story 003.0 are met.
